title: Temporal slab hinting and kernel prioritizer for paged-attention
creator: Anita Kapoor
description:
Goal: Reduce p95 total decode latency and memory churn for mid-to-large sequence workloads by combining a temporal slab hinting mechanism with a kernel prioritizer that biases short-path kernels for expected decode waves.

Context: We observe latency spikes during prefill->decode transitions for sequences >2k tokens when the paged KV cache has moderate fragmentation. Existing strategies either evict aggressively (hurting reuse) or conservatively (increasing memory pressure and slow kernel reads). Kernel selection today is reactive to measured tensor sizes; it doesn't account for anticipated prefill locality or imminent reuse windows.

This ticket implements: (1) a lightweight "temporal slab hint" metadata field on KV pages that records recent touch wave timestamps and decay score, (2) a slab-level prioritizer used by the kernel selection layer to prefer kernels with faster small-chunk decode paths when a page's hint signals imminent reuse, and (3) a scheduling hook that attempts soft pre-placements (non-blocking prefetch of high-probability slabs) coordinated with the runtime's decode wave scheduler.
acceptance_criteria:
- Implement slab hint store and decay policy with unit tests
- Kernel prioritizer influences kernel selection for at least 3 kernel candidates and falls back safely when priority path unavailable
- Integration test shows <=10% memory increase at peak compared to baseline while improving p95 decode latency by >=12% for 2k-4k token workloads
- No regression in overall throughput for short (<=256) sequences beyond 3%
- Telemetry exposes new metrics: slab_hint_score, prefetched_slab_count, kernel_priority_hits
technical_notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
1) Hint granularity: we store one decay score per slab (32-128KB) to keep metadata small. Per-slot hints were rejected because of metadata overhead.
2) Decay function: use exponential decay with half-life tuned to observed prefill cadence (~200ms for chat-style workloads). This avoids locking slabs as 'hot' for long chat sessions.
3) Kernel prioritizer policy: assign a numeric priority to kernels (short-path, quantized, fallback) and multiply by slab_hint_score to compute selection weight. To avoid pathological oscillation, add hysteresis window (50ms) before switching kernels for an active stream.
4) Prefetch strategy: soft prefetch uses the same admission controls as existing prefill but marked low-priority; prefetches may be preempted by higher-priority allocations.
5) Safety: prioritized kernel selection is advisory. Any kernel selection failure must fall back to the default path within the same request to avoid increased p95 tail due to missing kernels.

Implementation notes:
- Data structures: per-GPU slab_hint_array (float32) in contiguous buffer; updated by decode worker after each writeback/prefill.
- RPC surface: no API changes. All behavior lives inside the runtime.
- Telemetry: emit counters and histograms via existing metrics agent with tag {strategy: "temporal-hint"}.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for decay math and hint update in isolation.
2) Synthetic microbench: run synthetic prefill->decode scenarios with controlled fragmentation and compare kernel selection counts.
3) Integration perf run: 3-minute stable load using seq-lens [512, 1024, 2048, 4096], measure p50/p95/p99 decode end-to-end.
4) Regression: run standard long-run throughput test (100k reqs mixed-short) to validate <3% throughput regression.
5) Chaos: simulate kernel unavailability and confirm graceful fallback (no request hangs).
benchmarks: experiment v2 (hint + prioritizer + soft-prefetch): p95 decode (2k-4k) = 322ms (-15.7%)
memory peak change: +6% vs baseline in experiment v2 (within acceptance)

Suggested reviewers: @maria-chen, @tom-auerbach, @sre-oncall.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Over-eager prefetching amplifies memory pressure and evictions which can nullify latency gains. Mitigation: enforce admission tokens and a moving budget tied to free-residence headroom.
Risk: Mis-calibrated decay keeps slabs hot longer than they should for multi-tenant workloads. Mitigation: per-tenant decay calibration + safe defaults and opt-out config behind feature flag.
customer_notes: Customers running conversational workloads with long context windows may see reduced tail latency on decode-heavy paths with minor memory footprint increase. For Dedicated customers sensitive to memory, feature can be toggled per-tenant via runtime flag.
